chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the average of what one feeds his family. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'What you sustain your dependents with, from the average of that.' I said, 'And what is the average of that?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Vinegar, and oil, and dates, and bread, satiating them with it once.' I said, 'Their clothing?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One garment.'
ai.seo_question: What constitutes the average food and clothing for a family according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the concept of 'average' (wasat) sustenance for expiation purposes, identifying humble staples like vinegar, oil, dates, and bread as sufficient to satisfy a family once. This definition reflects the practical economic reality of the time, emphasizing modesty and sufficiency over luxury, which aligns with the Shia jurisprudential principle that expiation should be accessible to the average believer. The mention of a single garment further underscores the baseline requirement for clothing, highlighting simplicity in daily life.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the average of what one is feeding his family. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What you are sustaining your family with, from the average of that’. I said, ‘And what is the average of that’. I said, ‘And what is the average of that?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The vinegar, and the oil, and the dates, and the bread, satiating them by it, once’. I said, ‘Their clothing?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘One cloth’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about, ‘. . .

the average kind of food that you provide for your family.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the kind of food which you feed your family, it must be of the middle of the two, high and low, quality that you provide for your family.’ I then asked, ‘What is the middle of such food?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is vinegar and oil and dates and bread to satisfy them once.’ I then asked about clothing them. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is one piece of cloth.’”
